title: Investigate 'cueing' lag causing token throughput collapse for mixed-context workloads
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Production customers (mid-tier SaaS tenant X and an enterprise VPC customer) reported sudden degradation in tokens/sec and TTFT for workloads that mix short control tokens (<=20 tokens) with medium prompt segments (200-600 tokens). The regressions surfaced after the runtime kernel scheduler change rolled in 1.24.0 which attempted more aggressive preemption to improve throughput for long-context single-tenant jobs. Symptoms: (1) first-token latency spikes on multiplexed requests, (2) downstream bursts where token emission stalls for ~300-800ms before recovering, (3) higher variance in token/sec across identical requests. This ticket tracks triage, immediate customer mitigations, and a short hotfix for Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
steps_to_reproduce: Run mixed-length fanout workload: 60% requests with 12 token prompts + 40% with 400 token prompts, concurrency 120 across a multiplexed worker pool
Observe first-token latency distribution and tokens/sec measured on per-request tracing (use trace id header)
Toggle scheduler flag 'preempt_aggressive=true' to reproduce regression vs baseline=false
Reproduce on Dedicated cluster with 4xA100 and on a Hosted region to validate cross-deployment behavior
investigation_findings: Regression correlates to kernel-scheduler heuristics that preempt small inference batches to prioritize a recently queued long-context job; preemption frequency increased by ~3x after 1.24.0
KV-cache eviction windows were coincidentally aligned with scheduler preemption which caused repeated cache refills for mixed contexts and amplified stalls
Multiplex queue fairness leveraged time-slicing that did not account for short-control token priming patterns, leading to starvation bursts
Issue reproducible across Hosted and Dedicated; Private customers saw similar but lower magnitude impact due to different autoscaler warmup timing
mitigation_plan: Immediate: roll back scheduler heuristic flag to previous default on Hosted (runtime-1.24 revert of preempt_aggressive) and apply hotpatch to Dedicated clusters
Short-term: enable short-request hedging window (50ms) for mixed-length routing to prioritize finishing priming tokens
Introduce KV-cache grace period of 200ms after preemption to prevent aggressive eviction thrashing
Notify affected customers with mitigation timeline and provide temporary quota bump to Dedicated customers where rollback impacts throughput
decision: Approve emergency rollback of preempt_aggressive change for runtime-1.24.0 and ship runtime-1.24.2-hotfix with hedging + KV-cache grace. Iterate on a deterministic scheduler fairness model for the next cycle.
acceptance_criteria: Hosted: 95th percentile TTFT for mixed-context workload returns to baseline within 2 hours of rollback
Dedicated: controlled canary shows no tokens/sec stall under identical load (canary pass 1 hour)
Private: packaging provides clear patch with knob to disable preempt_aggressive and docs updated
Automated regression test added to CI that simulates mixed-length fanout and asserts tokens/sec stability
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Immediate): Roll back scheduler heuristic in hosted region us-west-2; monitor 5m/1m TTFT and token-emission traces
Step 2 (Canary): Patch 5 Dedicated pools with runtime-1.24.2-hotfix; run mixed-length synthetic load for 1 hour
Step 3 (Gradual): If canary stable, roll to remaining Dedicated pools over 4 hours with staggered windows; Private customers provided patch and instructions
Step 4 (Post-Deploy): 24h monitoring with automated SLA alert thresholds and rollback playbook ready
long_term_action_items: Design and implement deterministic scheduler fairness policy that factors in priming token lengths
Add KV-cache eviction telemetry and a simulation harness for mixed-length patterns
Enhance canary load generator to include mixed-length fanout scenarios for future releases
Evaluate kernel-level preemption knobs to reduce cross-tenant amplification
notes: Customer X called support 2025-11-12 09:14 UTC; provided temporary mitigation and committed rollback timeline
